cards.explanation: The reason is that the LORD has spoken. The verse says, “Do not be arrogant, for the LORD has spoken.” (Jeremiah 13:15) When God has spoken, a big head has nowhere to stand. My chef's hat is tall enough already, friends, and even I tip it down a little.

The answer is True. The verse says, “You wait for light, but He turns it into deep gloom and thick darkness.” (Jeremiah 13:16) Waiting on light and getting thicker dark is a heavy picture. I spent years in a dark junk drawer, so I know how long waiting for light can feel.

If the people don't listen, Jeremiah will weep in secret because of their pride. The verse says, “But if you do not listen, I will weep in secret because of your pride.” (Jeremiah 13:17) I think this is where you see how much Jeremiah, God's prophet, cares. He isn't gloating, friends, he's crying where nobody can see.

His eyes overflow because the LORD's flock has been taken captive. Jeremiah says, “My eyes will overflow with tears, because the LORD’s flock has been taken captive.” (Jeremiah 13:17) The flock means the LORD's people, taken away. That's a heavy part, and the tears are real.

The word is lowly. The king and the queen mother are told, “Take a lowly seat, for your glorious crowns have fallen from your heads.” (Jeremiah 13:18) The queen mother is the king's mother. I've been moved from the counter to the back of a drawer, so I know what a lowly seat feels like.

The answer is False. Jeremiah 13:19 says, “All Judah has been carried into exile, wholly taken captive.” Not a few towns, friends. All of Judah, wholly taken. The word doing the work there is “wholly.”

They are coming from the north. The message says, “Lift up your eyes and see those coming from the north.” (Jeremiah 13:20) It's a call to look up and see them coming. The verse names a direction and nothing more, so I'll leave it there.

The word is labor. The verse asks, “Will not pangs of anguish grip you, as they do a woman in labor?” (Jeremiah 13:21) It's a picture of anguish that grips them. It shows how deep the anguish will be.

The answer is False. The text says, “It is because of the magnitude of your iniquity that your skirts have been stripped off and your body has been exposed.” (Jeremiah 13:22) It doesn't say anything about enemies being too strong. It gives what to answer if they ask, “Why has this happened to me?”

The question says they can't do good when they're used to evil. The verse says, “Neither are you able to do good…” and then names them as people accustomed to doing evil. (Jeremiah 13:23) Ask a leopard to swap spots and you get a very patient look and no change. The question says that doing evil has become their habit.

The word is forgotten. The LORD says this is their lot “because you have forgotten Me and trusted in falsehood.” (Jeremiah 13:25) Forgetting Him and trusting falsehood go together in that sentence. It's a sad pair of words.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “…I have seen your detestable acts.” (Jeremiah 13:27) This is one of the heavy parts of the passage, and I won't make light of it. The LORD names what He has seen, and then He calls out, “Woe to you, O Jerusalem!”

He asks how long Jerusalem will remain unclean. The LORD says, “Woe to you, O Jerusalem! How long will you remain unclean?” (Jeremiah 13:27) It's the closing question, friends, left hanging at the end of the passage. The text doesn't answer it here.
